summary:
Our approach: We started from NASA's challenge and its five spaceflight hazards: radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, gravity, and closed environments. We asked how an astronaut could check their own health when ground replies take up to 22 minutes, and designed the tool around that.
What we're building: A digital twin of the astronaut's body. A 60-second daily check-in logs heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, sleep and mood. A clickable body then glows green, yellow or red, and each alert is linked to a NASA hazard so the astronaut learns why it changed. A smart escalation system advises: keep going, retest, or contact the flight surgeon with an auto-generated report. A mind companion watches mood and sleep for isolation stress.
What we've built so far: The full concept, a 6-slide presentation (PowerPoint and an online version), and a simulated 30-day Mars demo story.
How it helps: Astronauts can spot problems early, understand them in plain language, and act safely on long missions. Flight surgeons receive clear, ready-made reports.
details:
Health Max AI: Your Body's Digital Twin for Deep Space

Health Max AI is health monitoring software that gives astronauts a living digital twin of their own body. On long missions to the Moon and Mars, ground replies can take up to 22 minutes, so astronauts must assess and treat themselves. Health Max AI makes that simple.

Our team, APEX CODERZ, developed an AI-driven health intelligence system at the core of the app. In a 60-second daily check-in, astronauts log heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, sleep and mood. The AI analyzes these readings and their trends, then lights up a clickable 3D body in green, yellow or red. Each alert is linked to one of NASA's five spaceflight hazards, so the astronaut learns why the body is changing, not just that it is.

A smart escalation engine decides the next step: keep going, retest in six hours, or contact the flight surgeon with an auto-generated report. A mind companion tracks mood and sleep to catch isolation stress early. Mission Mode adapts advice for a spacecraft, Moon base or Mars rover, and gamified streaks keep astronauts engaged.

Health Max AI turns raw numbers into clear, explainable guidance, helping crews stay healthy when help is far away.
